text: Before approval: Testing mode is limited to 100 test users listed on the consent screen.
quote: Projects configured with a publishing status of Testing are limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.

text: Before approval: test-user authorizations and refresh tokens expire 7 days after consent.
quote: Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent. If your OAuth client requests an offline access type and receives a refresh token, that token will also expire.
note: Page exempts apps requesting only name/email/profile (openid) scopes.

text: Before approval: an In-production app requesting unapproved sensitive or restricted scopes shows the unverified app screen.
quote: Google will display an Unverified apps warning message if your project's OAuth clients request authorization of scopes considered sensitive or restricted before your project has completed verification

text: Before approval: unverified apps are capped at 100 new users for the lifetime of the project, and the cap cannot be reset.
quote: the user cap applies over the entire lifetime of the project, and it cannot be reset or changed.
note: FAQ ties the 100 new-user cap to unverified apps accessing sensitive or restricted scopes.

text: Verify ownership of your authorized domains in Google Search Console.
quote: Verify ownership of your project's authorized domains within the Google Search Console.

text: Host a public home page and a privacy policy on the same domain, both linked from the consent screen.
quote: The privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the same domain as your application's home page, and linked to on the OAuth consent screen of the Google API Console.
note: Home page must be publicly accessible; home page URI is part of the consent screen branding.

text: The privacy policy must disclose how the app accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data.
quote: The privacy policy must disclose the manner in which your application accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data.

text: Give a written justification for each sensitive scope, including why a narrower scope is not enough.
quote: Prepare a detailed justification for each requested sensitive scope, as well as an explanation for why a narrower scope isn't sufficient.

text: Submit an unlisted YouTube video showing the consent flow, the client ID in the address bar, and each scope in use.
quote: Upload the video to YouTube Studio and set its Visibility as Unlisted.
note: Page also requires showing the consent flow, the client ID in the address bar, and functionality of each sensitive scope.

text: You must publish your branding before you can request verification for data access.
quote: Note that you must have a published branding status before you can request verification for data access.

text: Internal-only apps (Workspace-owned project, Internal audience) skip verification and the 100-user cap but only work in that org.
quote: Your app will not be subject to the unverified app screen or the 100-user cap if it's designated as internal-only.
note: Page: 'only users in the Workspace or Cloud Identity organization will be able to use your app'; project must be org-owned with Internal consent screen.

text: spreadsheets and spreadsheets.readonly are sensitive; drive.file is the recommended non-sensitive scope.
quote: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file See, edit, create, and delete only the specific Google Drive files you use with this app. Recommended Non-sensitive
note: Same table lists spreadsheets and spreadsheets.readonly as Sensitive.

text: drive and drive.readonly also work with Sheets but are restricted, which adds a security assessment if you store or transmit the data on servers.
quote: If you store restricted scope data on servers (or transmit), then you must go through a security assessment.
note: Table lists drive and drive.readonly as Restricted.

text: Composio says its default OAuth app shares Sheets quota across users; your own app gets a dedicated quota.
quote: If you're using Composio's default OAuth app, you share that quota with other users, which can cause limits to be hit faster. Use your own OAuth app credentials to get a dedicated quota
note: Text is in the FAQ accordion (server-rendered payload).

text: Google's FAQ estimates sensitive scope verification at 10 business days, which is longer than the 3-5 days on the developer page.
quote: Sensitive Scope Verification
note: FAQ table lists Sensitive Scope Verification expected time as '10 Business days'; the 3-5 days figure is on the developers.google.com sensitive-scope page, verified separately.

text: Limits apply to refresh tokens: 100 per Google Account per client ID, and creating a new one silently invalidates the oldest.
quote: If the limit is reached, creating a new refresh token automatically invalidates the oldest refresh token without warning.
note: Preceding sentence: 'There is currently a limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per OAuth 2.0 client ID.'

text: Refresh tokens stop working after 6 months unused or if the user revokes access.
quote: The refresh token has not been used for six months.
note: Page also lists revocation, password change with Gmail scopes, token limit, time-based access, and admin policy.

text: Your OAuth redirect URI must exactly match oauth_redirect_uri in the Composio auth config; some defaults still use /api/v1/auth-apps/add.
quote: The redirect URI in your OAuth app must exactly match oauth_redirect_uri in your Composio auth config. Some toolkit defaults still use https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add

text: Use separate Google Cloud projects for testing and production, and submit only the production project for verification.
quote: Please create separate projects for development/testing/staging and production as per the Google OAuth policy.
note: Page also: 'You should only submit "production" tier projects for verification.'

text: Workspace admins can restrict sensitive scopes to OAuth clients they explicitly mark as trusted.
quote: Google Workspace organization administrators might restrict access to sensitive scopes to prevent access by OAuth client IDs that the organization doesn't explicitly mark as trusted.

text: Google OAuth sensitive scope verification for spreadsheets or spreadsheets.readonly | wait: 3-5 business days (Google's FAQ estimates 10)
quote: The sensitive scope verification process typically takes 3-5 business days to complete.
note: 10 business days figure is from the Google Cloud FAQ (answer/13463817).

text: Before listing: a marketplace-distribution app is limited to 25 installs, excluding developer test accounts.
quote: Marketplace OAuth app prior to listing: can be installed in up to 25 accounts (not including developer test accounts).

text: The 25-install cap applies to apps created or migrated on the Developer Platform from September 22, 2025.
quote: Starting on September 22nd, 2025, apps that are created or migrated to version 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until they are listed on the HubSpot Marketplace.
note: Applies to marketplace-distribution apps on Developer Platform version 2025.2 (platform launched Sep 3, 2025; enforcement began Sep 22).

text: Private-distribution apps can only be installed in up to 10 allowlisted accounts.
quote: Privately distributed OAuth apps: can be installed in up to 10 allowlisted accounts (not including developer test accounts).

text: Before review, installers see an unverified-app warning and must type "I accept the risk" to connect.
quote: Then type I accept the risk, and click Connect to authorize the app.
note: Applies until the app is verified by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team.

text: New apps are created with the HubSpot CLI (v7.6.0) via `hs project create`, with redirect URLs and scopes in app-hsmeta.json.
quote: Make sure you're using v7.6.0 of the HubSpot CLI before proceeding.
note: Page uses hs project create; redirectUrls and requiredScopes live in app-hsmeta.json.

text: Production redirect URLs must use HTTPS.
quote: For production applications, https is required.

text: Listing needs at least three active installs in unaffiliated production accounts with activity in the past 30 days.
quote: Active installs are the number of unique HubSpot production accounts, unaffiliated with your organization, showing successful app activity within the past 30 days.
note: Page: 'at least three active, unique installs'.

text: Listing needs live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs, a support contact, and a public setup guide.
quote: URLs for your app's Terms of Service and Privacy Policy must be live and up-to-date.
note: Page also requires public setup documentation and at least one support contact method.

text: Listed apps must use OAuth as the only auth method and request only the scopes they need.
quote: OAuth: your app must use OAuth as its sole authorization method.
note: Page: 'Scopes: only request scopes your app needs.'

text: Listed AI connectors must require user-level permissions or be built with HubSpot's MCP Server.
quote: it must require user-level permissions by setting access to user-level or be built with HubSpot's MCP Server.

text: Access tokens currently expire after 30 minutes, so the refresh flow must work.
quote: The access token will expire after the number of seconds given in the expires_in field of the response, currently 30 minutes.

text: You can submit only one app for listing at a time; extra submissions are rejected automatically.
quote: you can only submit one app at a time for approval. Any additional apps submitted while the initial app is being processed will automatically be rejected.

text: Composio's managed HubSpot app is still awaiting HubSpot approval, so users see a warning; your own app avoids that once listed.
quote: HubSpot shows this warning because the default Composio-managed HubSpot OAuth app is still awaiting HubSpot approval.
note: Text is in the FAQ accordion (server-rendered payload).

text: Composio's managed app cannot add scopes; a different scope set needs your own app.
quote: You cannot add new scopes to the managed app
note: Page: 'If you need a different scope set, create a custom HubSpot OAuth app'.

text: $0; no listing fee is stated in the listing requirements
note: Absence claim: the page mentions no fee, cost or price; '$0' is an inference, not stated.

text: Private apps get no Marketplace listing page but can be shared with any Pipedrive company via an unlisted install link.
quote: Live private apps can be shared with any user/company in Pipedrive via a direct, unlisted installation link

text: You need a developer sandbox account to access the Developer Hub.
quote: Request a developer sandbox account to get access to the Developer Hub

text: Both private and public apps must use OAuth 2.0 with working install and uninstall flows.
quote: All apps (public and private) should manage authentication and authorization using OAuth 2.0 and, subsequently, enable a smooth installation and uninstallation.
note: Page says 'should'; installation flows are called mandatory.

text: Public apps need Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages and agreement to the Developer Partner Agreement.
quote: Your app has a Terms of Service webpage with clearly stated rules that users must agree to abide by to use your service
note: Checklist also: 'You agree with the Pipedrive Developer Partner Agreement'.

text: Public app review needs a demo video, up-to-date test accounts, and 3-5 listing images.
quote: Your app listing includes 3-5 high-quality images
note: App review checklist also requires a demo video and fully functional, up-to-date test accounts.

text: The callback URL in requests must match the one entered when registering the app.
quote: Authorization code will be sent to that URL (if it matches with the value you entered in the registration form)

text: The app type (private or public) cannot be changed later in Developer Hub.
quote: NB: Do pick your app type carefully, as it cannot be changed later on Developer Hub.

text: Every user in a company installs the app separately; installs are per user.
quote: Every user in a company needs to install or set up their own apps and integrations.

text: Access tokens last 60 minutes; refresh tokens expire after 60 days unused, forcing a full reinstall.
quote: refresh_token will expire if it isn't used in 60 days.
note: Page: 'access_token expires after 60 minutes' and the whole installation process must restart after refresh token expiry.

text: Approved public apps are unlisted by default and must be published manually.
quote: The app is unlisted from the Marketplace by default after approval.

text: Don't click Install and Test in Pipedrive; start the connection from Composio and enter the company subdomain.
quote: Do not start the user connection by clicking Install and Test inside Pipedrive's OAuth app settings.
note: Page: start the connection from Composio and enter the Pipedrive subdomain when prompted.

text: "App not found" usually means the client ID/secret don't match or the app isn't available to that user.
quote: Pipedrive usually shows "App not found" when the OAuth app used for the connection is not approved or available for that user/workspace.
fix: "App not found" usually means the OAuth app isn't approved or available for that user; also check that the client ID and secret belong to the same app.
note: Page gives 'not approved/available' as the usual cause; mismatched client ID/secret is only a troubleshooting check.

text: $0; no submission or listing fee is mentioned
note: Absence claim: the page mentions no fee, cost or price; '$0' is an inference, not stated.

text: 300 requests per 10 seconds per API key and 100 per 10 seconds per token.
quote: There is a limit of 300 requests per 10 seconds for each API key and 100 requests per 10 second interval for each token.

text: Requests to /1/members/ are limited to 100 per 900 seconds.
quote: Additionally, there is a limit on requests to /1/members/ of 100 requests per 900 seconds.

text: An API key is tied to a Power-Up created in the admin portal at trello.com/apps/admin.
quote: As an API key is tied to a Power-Up, you can visit the https://trello.com/apps/admin page

text: The Power-Up must be owned by a Trello Workspace.
quote: The Trello Workspace that owns the app.
note: Page describes the Workspace field for any app, including Power-Ups.

text: The app form asks for an email, a support email and an author name.
quote: Support Email We'll use this email when questions arise from users regarding your app
note: Create form fields include Name, Workspace, Email, Support Email and Author.

text: OAuth 1.0 signing needs the application secret from the Trello Auth tab.
quote: You'll also need your application secret (used to sign your requests). That's listed in the Trello Auth tab

text: If the API key has no allowed origins set, no redirect URL works.
quote: Note: If your API key has no allowed origins set, then no redirect URL will work.

text: Redirects to a return_url not in allowed origins are blocked.
quote: If the URL in the return_url parameter does not match one of your API key's allowed origins, the redirect is blocked.

text: Token expiration can be 1hour, 1day, 30days or never.
quote: 1hour, 1day, 30days, never

text: Scopes are only read, write and account.
quote: Comma-separated list of one or more of read, write, account.

text: By default only admins of the owning Workspace can manage the app.
quote: By default, apps can only be managed by admins of the Workspace that owns the Power-Up.

text: Composio's Trello toolkit uses OAuth 1, not OAuth 2.
quote: OAuth1
note: Toolkit page lists only OAuth1 as auth scheme (authSchemes: OAUTH1); it does not explicitly say 'not OAuth 2'.

text: Rate limit is per token: 100 requests/min on Free, Unlimited and Business plans.
quote: The ClickUp API applies rate limits per token.
note: Table: FreeForever 100, Unlimited 100, Business 100 requests per minute per token.

text: Business Plus gets 1,000 and Enterprise 10,000 requests per minute per token.
quote: Business Plus 1,000 Enterprise / Enterprise Plus 10,000
note: Enterprise row is 'Enterprise / Enterprise Plus'.

text: Only Workspace owners or admins can create OAuth apps.
quote: Only Workspace owners or admins can create OAuth apps.

text: Create the app under Settings > Apps with a name and redirect URL.
quote: Name the app and add a redirect URL.
note: Path: avatar > Settings > Apps > Create new app.

text: Access tokens currently do not expire, but ClickUp says this may change.
quote: The access token currently does not expire. This is subject to change.

text: Non-SSL redirect URIs may not be supported in the future.
quote: Non-SSL redirect URIs may not be supported in the future.

text: Users pick one or more Workspaces at authorization; re-authorize to change them.
quote: Users can authorize one or more Workspaces.
note: Page: 'Redirect users to the authorization URL to modify Workspace permissions.'
